plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: Tall stems carry broad daisy-like blooms. Drooping rose-purple petals surround a spiky, copper-orange central cone. In the summer prairie, bees and butterflies crowd onto the flowers, and goldfinches come later for the seeds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early July to mid-August, so July 28 falls within the season
plants.location: Tallgrass prairies and woodland edges of the central and eastern United States, such as Iowa
plants.funFact: The spiky central cone is a dense cluster of tiny true flowers. The petal-like rays around it are separate ray florets.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of tiny violet-blue flowers. On warm days they fill the fields of Provence with a sweet, herbal scent, and the rows look like purple corduroy rolling across the hills.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-June to late August, with peak bloom in July, so it is still flowering on July 28
plants.funFact: Lavender takes its name from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans used it to scent baths and laundry.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest of all the proteas, it has a goblet-sized flower head. Its crown of pink, silky-tipped bracts surrounds a fuzzy center. It blooms in the middle of the Southern Hemisphere winter, among the fynbos of the Cape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly winter and spring, June to October, so July 28 is within the season
plants.location: Fynbos shrublands of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa, including the Kirstenbosch gardens in Cape Town
plants.funFact: It is South Africa's national flower. Its thick underground stem lets it survive the wildfires that regularly sweep the fynbos.
